info.desc: Boy is the debut studio album by Irish rock band U2. It was produced by Steve Lillywhite and was released on 20 October 1980 by Island Records. Boy contains songs from the band's 40-song repertoire at the time, including two tracks that were re-recorded from their original versions on the group's debut release, the EP Three. Boy was recorded from July to September 1980 at Dublin's Windmill Lane Studios, which became U2's chosen recording location during the 1980s. It was their first time working with Lillywhite, who employed non-standard production techniques, such as recording drummer Larry Mullen Jr. playing in .

podcast.body: Before the creation of their debut album, "Boy," a young and then-unknown U2 visited Strawberry Studios in search of a producer. It was during this time that they encountered Joy Division, who were in the process of recording. "estaban buscando productor para lo que va a ser subrimer algo... para lo que fue el Boy."

podcast.body: U2's debut album, *Boy*, was released as a special, limited edition on white vinyl during the Black Friday component of Record Store Day in 2020. This particular version was restricted to a production run of just 10,000 copies. "I am a special copy of U2's debut album, Boy, that was part of the Black Friday part of record store day in 2020. It's on white vinyl and was limited to just 10,000 copies."

podcast.body: U2's debut album, which featured their first major single "I Will Follow." A Deluxe reissue of the album was released in 2008, including previously hard-to-find or unavailable material, such as an early version of "I Will Follow" from 1980. "U2's first big single of course was, I will follow from the Boy album."
